Lisinopril and Angioedema
Been on Lisinopril 20mg for 5yrs  absolutely no side effects or issues. It really helped lower my BP. Woke up Sun 11/10 w/bottom lip swelling. I took it as eczema which I have and treated my lip. Tues 11/12 top lip swollen still thought eczema. Wed 11/13 Dr. appt and she called 911 because she said it’s not eczema I have an allergic reaction to something. Got to ED, ran tests, Dr said my allergic reaction is 99% caused by Lisinopril 🤯 I asked how when I’ve been on it 5 yrs with no issues. He explained with Lisinopril (ACE inhibitors) allergic reaction can happen years into being on it. It happens to some patients . I had a delayed reaction. He said if I waited for one more day and took my daily morning dose, my throat would’ve started to close. No more ACE inhibitors for me ever! So thankful my case was mild and I was seen sooner than later. Just wanted to spread the word about allergic reactions to this med and many others. It can happen no matter how long you’ve been taking them. Any symptoms of allergic reaction even mild ones go to the ED or call 911. Don’t wait or self diagnosis. Take care!

anxiety or more? 

39F- 5’0, 135 lbs. 
DX: anxiety, panic disorder, PTSD, high bp, anemia, GERD, idiopathic constipation. 

Medications: Celexa, Klonopin (PRN,) Protonix, Linzess, iron supplement, Lisinopril (PRN.) 

Surgeries: 3 c-sections, hysterectomy, oophorectomy (I have one remaining ovary,) and VSG. 

I will try to keep this as short as possible. For the past month or so, I’ve been having episodes of what I can only explain as PVCs. I feel like my heart is fluttering or skipping a beat. I have had these before (w/ anxiety,) but these feel different to me. A few times when they have happened, I have had dizzy spells afterwards but that only lasts for 15-30 seconds. The fluttering lasts on and off for a few minutes every couple hours, but there have also been days where I’ve had none. I have seen a cardiologist in the past when I was first diagnosed w/ high BP (3 years ago.) I also had an abnormal EKG (although I’m not sure what was abnormal about it.)  He did a stress test, echo, kidney u/s, and holter monitor. After all the tests came back normal, he had me do at home bp checks for 3 months, he came to the conclusion that my high bp was due to anxiety/stress. On days my anxiety isn’t bad, my bp is actually on the lower side, but when my anxiety is high, it’s high, but w/ Lisinopril (10 mg.,) it is stabilized. He prescribed me the Lisinopril to take as needed, so I check my bp daily. 

With I saw my PCP recently about this, he didn’t seem too concerned, but he did refer me  back to my cardiologist, but I can’t get in until February. He also referred me for another holter monitor test, this time it will be 48 hrs. I showed him the few EKGs I have that I took from my apple watch and he didn’t say much. My fiancé (who’s an RN) told me they look like PVCs, but he can’t be certain. This, of course, fuels my anxiety and makes it worse, but I know he’s not a cardiologist or doctor and isn’t qualified to diagnose. I’ve never posted here before, so I apologize if my post has too many details/not enough. I should add that I lost both my parents suddenly to heart attacks. my mom was 60, my dad was 62. My dad had CAD and high cholesterol. He had his first heart attack at 41 followed by bypass surgery. He lived a beautiful and happy life for 21 more years, and passed suddenly. My mom had a stroke at 55 due to high bp which she was diagnosed in her 40’s w/. She couldn’t afford her bp meds which led to her stroke. After a couple of months in the hospital/rehab, she did well for a few years until she, once again, couldn’t afford her medications/regular doctor visits, and she passed suddenly from a heart attack at home Their deaths were very traumatic for me, which only adds to my fear. After my mom’s death, I took my health very seriously. I lost 110 lbs., and maintained it for 7 yrs., and I also quit smoking. I want to live a long happy/healthy life. Something, both of my parents were robbed from. I know PVCs can be harmless, and many times, they are, however, the dizzy spells and frequency of them worry me. I would always rather know of a health problem than not. Early detection is vital for anyone’s outcome. I have included a few of my EKGs from my Apple watch. I really appreciate any input, even if you can’t give me much. Again- thank you so much.

When to worry about diarrhea, C Diff, Gastritis, Pancreatitis, or Gastroenteritis?
Hello, 39M here with relatively well controlled high blood pressure (lisinopril 20mg 1x day) , cerebral palsy (tizanidine (usually 4mg 2-3 x daily), (what I was told about 18 months ago was) mild fatty liver, and anxiety (buspirone 15mg 3-4 x daily).

I've been having diarrhea or loose stools now for about 2 or 3 of the last 4 days. My wife also had a stomach bug that lasted about 6 days the week prior to me getting sick. I took an Imodium on the first day that seemed to help later the first day/night after having several bouts of diarrhea, and a second does later in the morning on the second day (after a first morning bout) that kept me much more somewhat regular/normal on day 2 and a lot of day 3, except for some mild stomach cramps, and I ate my normal semi-keto low carb eggs, meat and veggies diet.

Last night (day/night 3) I ate a side salad with ranch, some grilled chicken tenders, and a little bit of cooked spinach and started having slightly worse moderate stomach cramps and another bout of diarrhea. After that I fasted for 18 hours until lunch today, where I had a bowl of chicken broth, a half serving of many salted pretzel sticks, and one small breaded frozen air-fried chicken tender. For dinner I had 5 grilled chicken wings, unsauced, seasoned with just salt and pepper and a little garlic powder, and some cooked green beans.

I've had diarrhea about 6 times today (day 4). However, twice now in the last two hours I've passed small amounts of stool and **yellow liquid** about the color of darker urine. Any stool so far has all been normal brown to orange-ish or light brown and maybe a few pieces were slightly green occasionally. No obvious signs of blood, black stool, etc.

I have an appetite, no fever, no other symptoms as far as I know, urinating regularly, no obvious signs of dehydration, etc.

All that said, while I know it could likely be the same thing my wife had or gastritis from drinking, I'm also worried I may have C diff as 1. I just finished a 10 day dose of amox-clav 15 days ago (for a mild skin infection as a precaution from a small puncture/paronychia that ultimately healed fine) and about 30 days ago I had a couple of bouts of semi-sweet or fruity smelling BMs and gas after a night of drinking, and, 2. I've also been a moderate to heavy nightly drinker (5-6 drinks most nights to cope with some CP pain, anxiety) for the last 5-6 years. The other concern I have is its pancreatitis or something to do with my liver from drinking too much, especially since I drank on the night before I got sick.

I haven't drank since the night before I got sick, and am finally got to a good place in the last several weeks where I've started to cut back on my drinking and plan on doing so even more going forward after the first of the year.

Should I be concerned its something more than simple gastritis or gastroenteritis that my wife also had recently, and if I should wait before going to get checked out, how long should I wait if I'm continuing to have symptoms? Any ideas or feedback is much appreciated.

Please keep in mind that my heart rate before going on Atenolol was lower, roughly around 65-70 bpm at rest. What are your experiences or thoughts?

* Where else should we be looking?

I worked as a researcher at a hospital so naturally they called a code blue, and had me transported from one building to another on the medical campus.

My third and final seizure happened about 2 years after the first one. I was about to leave to go to work from a girlfriend's house. Similar story, she called an ambulance, I e-mailed her later to get details which matched up with this.

I have had CAT scan, MRIs, Echocardiograms, EEG, done a tilt-table experiment and worn a halter monitor. The halter monitor was weakly suggestive of sleep apnea, and I snore and have a thick neck, but no evidence of arrthymia. Overall there no evidence of heart problems in syncope or gross anatomical damage to the brain.

After my third incident I was prescribed lamotrigine, slowly went up to 150 mg x 2 daily, and I've been taking it since at that dose (so, close to 8 years), with no loss of consciousness although there are times I feel a bit "off" without being able to discribe the feeling well to my partner or the neurologists. I have chosen to continue taking it, started driving again about 2 years after my most recent seizure (so in 2014), but won't swim, hike on narrow trails, rarely cross the street against traffic, or do other activities where I would have zero protection if I had another seizure.

I don't believe I've had more than 4 drinks in a night, or for 1-2 drinks, less than 3 times in a week. I have avoided alcohol even more since taking the Lamotrigine given that it can increase propensity for drowsiness, and in any case was not drinking more than 1-2 times a week 1-2 drinks, around the time of the incidents or drinking more than usual.

One year today since my last severe panic attack and ER visit. 
Hi all,

I’m sharing this hoping that it will help someone stumbling through Reddit as I had many times looking for hope and explanations to the very physical symptoms that started happening. 

At 37 years old (male), I balanced a stressful career, started a side hustle that grew to 6 employees (while keeping my day job), raising kids, and being the best husband I could. 

I honestly don’t know if it was pent up childhood trauma, fears, hormones, aging, or grief, but in May of 2023, I had an absolutely debilitating panic attack out of nowhere. I just lost my dad to cancer in April 2023 and about one month later, I found myself driving, listening to a podcast, drinking coffee, and generally having a great day without a care in the world… Never taken any medications, was slightly overweight but active, and never been to therapy or had any anxiety. Honestly, I could not empathize with what people experience until it happened to me. 

All of the sudden, a sharp pain zapped where I imagined my heart to be. It hit again, and again. I started feeling tingling in my hands and lips. I turned the air vent on my face and tried to catch my breathe. Was I passing out? Was I having a heart attack? Got a few palpitations… As I pulled off the interstate into the first town, I slowed down not knowing if I would make it. I came to a stop and texted my wife then Google the nearest hospital. I got zapped with another series of sharp pains in my chest and feeling like this was it… I pulled up the ER, ran in, and said I was having chest pain. The gave me an EKG, X-ray, took my labs, and BP. Besides having 160/90 BP and heart rate of 110, they said there was nothing wrong and sent me home. 

That was one of the worst days of my life. I didn’t realize it that day, but I was just introduced to my first panic attack. 

That entire week I felt off. My chest was sore, I was dizzy, and kept having the occasional palpitation. I followed up with Dr convinced I just had something wrong with my heart. 

All tests came back negative for any heart problems beyond my nagging high BP and faster heart rate. I never suffered high BP like this before…

Without any effort, I lost 30 pounds over the next two months, could not sleep much, could not focus on work, and all I thought about was dying or having another episode again. Between May-September 3rd, I would end up going to the ER 5 more times. It always hit me during non-stressful moments without any emotional trigger. It was like when my mind finally relaxed, my nervous system cracked the whip and said nope! 

I did notice mornings were better than afternoons/evenings. After that last trip to the ER exactly one year ago, I have never experienced a full blown panic attack that mimicked a heart attack ever again. Here is what worked for me to live life again and start healing:

1) I bought a blood pressure monitor and my Dr got me on lisinopril. I noticed my anxiety was sending everything through the roof. The BP meds treated both the BP and helped tone down the intensity of my physical panic episodes. 

2) I have not taken any other meds specifically for anxiety but I was one more panic attack from trying! If you need help, ask your Dr about it. 

3) I got as many tests as I could to give me peace of mind. I had a calcium score of zero, a CT Angiogram, Echo stress test, and ended up doing 5 more EKGs and labs. Beyond my BP, I had no other risk factors. 

4) Cut out caffeine to ZERO and reintroduce slowly. I’ll now do up to one small cup of black coffee per day. I mostly drink Dandelion or chamomile tea if I want something hot. 

5) I supplement with turkey tail & reishi mushroom powder in my tea, magnesium, D3, Vit C, Zinc, and I drink electrolyte mix in at least one glass of lemon water each morning when I first wake up. 

6) I wake up early at the same time each day now regardless of work or holidays. I don’t touch my phone or watch anything for an hour. I get up, drink the water, go outside, and take some deep slow breathes. I spend time with my thoughts and do some stretches and try to relax for a bit before any coffee or work or responsibilities. 

I still have anxiety. It strangely still hits me most commonly while I’m driving somewhere… After the first episode I didn’t drive more than 1 hour distance for 6 months…then I made it on a 3 hour road trip. Then I made it back. I started telling myself I’m not going to die, and just breathe when the waves hit. 

The strangest thing to me about this journey is how physical it is…it’s about 99% physical for me and not emotional or what I thought “anxiety” would feel like.   Fears and things out of your control make symptoms worse. For me, it’s important spending time each morning resetting my nervous system and bringing some control back into my day. 

Eating better, working out, and cutting stimulants, caffeine, drinking, etc…helps too. I notice the day after I have some drinks I usually feel some anxiety and mild palpitations. 

I share all this because it has been a year and I’m grateful. Not 100% clear of symptoms yet, but hopefully you can read this and know that you don’t have to give up. You can fight this! I’ve heard cognitive behavioral therapy is good, and getting a routine dialed in… Anybody else made progress on reversing panic disorder and anxiety? Would love to hear what’s working for you.

My Anxiety Story
I am now 33 years old, I started having anxiety only about 3 years ago and it is fairly infrequent. The first year it started around the Holiday period, I was drinking quite heavily every weekend for about 2-3 months before the anxiety started, a major cause of my anxiety was actually high blood pressure. The anxiety was so bad I had to take a month off work and move back in with my parents, and I originally didn't even know the issue was anxiety, I had just thought it was only because of the extremely high blood pressure. After that month things started to get back to normal. I went about 8-9 months anxiety free, or very little anxiety. During that first stretch of anxiety my doctor put me on blood pressure medication, such as Lisinopril and Lebetalol. I am currently still on Lisinopril.  


After my first stretch with anxiety, around October of the following year, I decided to smoke weed occasionally because I was getting bored with my non-work life. I smoked for about 2-3 months, then around Christmas I started having light chest rumbling all the time. It was from my blood pressure issues, I knew it. I quit weed but it was already too late, after a late night panic attack which resulted in an ambulance ride to the hospital, just a day before Christmas Eve, my anxiety kicked in again. I was again at my parents, in my comfort zone, for about a month and a half. I only took a week off during that period and continued to work through most of it. My anxiety always comes with increased heart rate, blood pressure and thoughts of heart attack, stroke, doom, etc.  


As of about 3 weeks ago, feeling great but also kinda bored again, I decided to go back to smoking weed at nights. Go figure that would kick off a new streak of anxiety after only 2 weeks. As of about a week ago I have been having bad anxiety, increased heart rate and blood pressure again, although I have gotten much better at managing it and I can still function daily. Some nights take 2-3 hours to fall asleep, some nights are instant sleep. It seems like my day to day life is a wild rollercoaster and I cannot wait for these episodes to finally end.  


I just wanted to get this off my chest after finding r/anxiety.

My Type 2 Diabetes Journey (Remission in 7 Months)

I’m long winded but I think this info is crucial as it paints the whole picture. :)

Growing up (child - 25ish years of age): Mom under-ate but loved junk food. Dad overate everything. I liked junk plus overate: constantly living with feelings of “enjoying/indulging->then regret/guilt”. I’m adopted so I have no family health history to lean on. 

Age 25ish-30: I became pescatarian (vegetarian + seafood) after a year of a disturbed gut. It worked! I started dating my now husband. We’d eat out a lot. When we got married, we moved to a big city. We both dealt with extreme stress and overworking at our jobs so eating out most nights was not only convenient but also a retreat in a way. It started catching up with us in weight. But I noticed I was gaining significantly more than him. 

Age 31-33: was only going to urgent care when “little illnesses” would arise (Covid, flue, etc). Nurses would mention my blood pressure was high but thought it was probably nerves. Wasn’t going to doctor for a physical yearly, like I should’ve been, because I felt fine. Did get migraines often. Noticed blurry vision sometimes, so eye doctor prescribed low prescription glasses. Noticed sometimes wounds in my feet or legs wouldn’t heal as quick and leave scars. Had a weird itchy/flaky patches of skin on my back and sides of breasts but dermatologist blamed sweating and gave me treatment that didn’t work. I had dry heels that cracked bad too. 

Age 34 (7 months ago): we move again and have a calming, stress-free change in lifestyles with our jobs. Giving us time to focus on life and health. We start eating Keto. Found a primary doctor. They ran routine bloodwork and I got a call with my Dr saying “has anyone told you that you have type 2 diabetes?”. In shock, I said no and she basically said “watch the consumption of candies, cakes, and things like white rice and we will follow up soon.” She gave me Metformin and Lisinopril (for high blood pressure) and said she’d see me in 2 months. I obviously freaked out and cried thinking I was dying or doomed because I didn’t know anything about t2d. 

After diagnosis: I did TONS of research trying to find a way to heal instead of cope/deal with it. Began Metformin and Lisinopril. The first 2 weeks were hell on earth. Lisinopril made me have to sleep every other hour and I had a foggy brain all the time. Couldn’t drive. Metformin was fine for a minute but then I ate something heavy with tomato paste and literally lived in the bathroom toilet+throwing up) consistently for 6 hours. Truly thought I was going to die. Found out (for me) highly acidic foods, especially at night, would make me have these issues while taking Metformin. Then everything regulated and I was good for the most part. I kept a log of what I’d eat each meal, plus my blood pressure and glucose readings. Highly recommend! Below I’ll share what ended up working. 

Now: Since diagnosis (7 months ago) I have lost over 50 lbs. Here’s what worked for me:
*started at 210lbs // now 157lbs (my non diabetic husband also lost 40lbs so it reassured that Metformin helped me start regulating my glucose but not be my cause of weight loss)
*high blood pressure is now sustained to normal levels at all times
*starting A1C was 8.5 // now 5.4
*my fasting glucose is usually 85-97, but usually in the 80s.
*exercise: walk my dog 2-5 miles a day trying to do hills where I can. Going to the gym when I can to do resistance training on my full body of muscles for overall strength. I like to walk after meals when I can to reduce glucose spikes. 
*food: This was key for me. We enjoy lots of good, hearty, carb-friendly meals but focusing on keeping saturated fats at 0 or very, very low. Avoiding refined carbs like white flour and white rice. No meat but I do eat fish with good fats and cholesterol (ex: Salmon). Avoiding things with “added sugar” (refined sugar). But equally important, we say yes to high fiber (especially when eating carbs), whole carbs (brown rice, whole wheat, etc.), lots of veggies and fruits prepared in all different ways, beans, and some healthy fat fish. I still drink coffee, tons of water, sparking water, and unsweet tea. When shopping for food, knowing to look for low saturated fat and no refined sugar as the base of finding good foods made it easy and way less stressful.

 My relationship with food has totally changed. I don’t feel bound to what I’m eating next. I don’t crave sugar like I did. I don’t feel guilt about my meals or if I treat myself on a special occasion or an event with a slice of cake or some French fries - and my body has gone into remission so my glucose says level, even after those treats now. I just challenge myself “is this treat worth it? Something you just have to have”? And reflect on my past few weeks - if I’ve had other treats or meals like that. Because it can add up if you’re not thinking about it. Plus we don’t buy things like that to bring home and eat. I don’t have THAT much self control 😂 but it’s so easy to say “no” now, while still saying “yes” to other times. I love it. 

Come July, for my check-in, hopefully I’ll be fully off Metformin and Lisinopril! 🤞🏻oh - and about 1 month ago, I started reducing my Metformin to 1 pill per day instead of two because I think it was working too hard and causing veryyy slow digestion and constipation (I was miserable with gut trouble for a few months). So for anyone out there experiencing the opposite trouble that Metformin causes with digestion, here you go. It’s now much better since the reduction. I’m also curious if it’s causing this eczema on my hand. Hmm. 

Hope this was helpful and encouraging for someone out there! Happy to answer any questions!
